question.text: In an experiment of measuring the refractive index of a glass slab using travelling microscope in physics lab, a student measures real thickness of the glass slab as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and apparent thickness of the glass slab at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. Travelling microscope has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> divisions in one <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> on main scale and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> divisions on Vernier scale is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>49</mn></math> divisions on main scale. The estimated uncertainty in the measurement of refractive index of the slab is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______

solution.text:
Given: 

50 VSD=49MSD⇒1VSD=4950MSD

So least count will be

=1MSD-1VSD=120 cm-4950·120 cm

=150×120 cm=0.01 mm

As we know, μ=hh'=5.255.00

Applying log on both sides, we get

lnμ=lnh–lnh’

Differentiating both sides, we get

dμμ=dhh-dh'h'

For calculation, all errors will be added, therefore

dμ=0.015.25+0.015.00μ

=4110×10-3

Hence, x=41
